title: The Pilgrim Sets Out
subtitle: John Bunyan's Pilgrim's Progress, Part 1
description: Begin the month with the most influential Puritan allegory ever written. Follow Christian as he flees the City of Destruction, falls into the Slough of Despond, and finds his burden loosed at the Cross.

title: The Discipline of Daily Prayer
subtitle: Practical Counsel on the Prayer Life
description: The Puritans were people of prayer. Receive their practical counsel on establishing fixed times, praying with Scripture, praying with honesty, persistence, and expectation.

title: Justification by Faith Alone
subtitle: The Doctrine of Justification
description: The article upon which the church stands or falls. Explore the Puritan understanding of how God declares sinners righteous through the imputed righteousness of Christ, received by faith alone.

title: The Bruised Reed
subtitle: Richard Sibbes and the Tenderness of Christ
description: Richard Sibbes's beloved classic on Isaiah 42:3 — Christ will not break the bruised reed nor quench the smoking flax. A word of profound comfort for every struggling believer.

title: The Pursuit of Holiness
subtitle: Practical Counsel on Personal Sanctification
description: The Puritans pursued holiness with their whole hearts. Receive their counsel on mortifying sin, cultivating the means of grace, relying on the Spirit, and finding joy in godliness.

title: The Doctrine of Sanctification
subtitle: Progressive Holiness in the Believer's Life
description: Sanctification is God's ongoing work of renewal — mortification of sin and vivification of holiness, changing believers from glory to glory into the image of Christ by the Spirit.

title: All Things for Good
subtitle: Thomas Watson on Romans 8:28
description: Watson's beloved treatise unpacking how all things — the best, the worst, and even sin itself — work together for the good of those who love God. A book for the suffering.

title: The Whole Armour of God
subtitle: Practical Counsel on Spiritual Warfare
description: Drawing from William Gurnall and the Puritans: know your enemy, put on the armour, wield the sword of the Spirit, pray always, and stand firm. The battle is real but the victory is certain.

title: The Doctrine of Divine Providence
subtitle: God's Sovereign Government of All Things
description: God upholds, directs, and governs all creatures and events. Explore the Puritan understanding of preservation, concurrence, and government — and how providence produces trust and patience.

title: Keeping the Heart
subtitle: John Flavel on the Inner Life
description: Flavel's searching treatise on Proverbs 4:23 — the heart as the command center of the soul, and the diligent keeping required in seasons of prosperity, adversity, temptation, and dryness.

title: The Rare Jewel of Christian Contentment
subtitle: Jeremiah Burroughs on Contentment
description: Burroughs defines contentment as a sweet, inward, quiet frame of spirit that freely submits to God's disposal. Learn to draw satisfaction from God rather than circumstances.

title: The Covenant of Grace
subtitle: God's Unbreakable Promise to His People
description: The foundational framework of Puritan theology: the covenant of works, the covenant of grace, and the glorious truth that God's relationship with His people rests on His faithfulness, not ours.

title: The Mortification of Sin
subtitle: John Owen's Classic on Killing Sin
description: Owen's most important practical work: if sin is not being killed in your life, it is killing you. Learn the seven steps of mortification — from identifying the enemy to fixing the heart on Christ.

title: The Ministry of Encouragement
subtitle: Building Up the Body of Christ
description: The Puritan vision of paraklesis — coming alongside to strengthen. Five forms of encouragement: presence, Scripture, testimony, practical help, and honest love.

title: The Doctrine of Eschatology
subtitle: Death, Judgment, Heaven, and Hell
description: The Puritan understanding of the last things: death as transition, judgment as accountability, heaven as the beatific vision, and hell as the seriousness of the Gospel.

title: The Religious Affections
subtitle: Jonathan Edwards on True and False Religion
description: Edwards's penetrating analysis of genuine faith: the signs that do not reliably indicate salvation, the signs that do, and the supreme importance of Christian practice as evidence of grace.

title: The Art of Meditation
subtitle: The Lost Discipline of Biblical Meditation
description: The Puritans were master meditators. Learn their methods of deliberate, occasional, and ejaculatory meditation — filling the mind with God's truth until the soul is transformed.

title: The Perseverance of the Saints
subtitle: The Security of the Believer
description: Those whom God has truly saved will be kept by His power unto final salvation. Explore the grounds of perseverance: God's eternal purpose, covenant, Christ's intercession, and the Spirit's seal.

title: The Valley of Vision
subtitle: The Rich Treasury of Puritan Prayer
description: Explore the Puritan tradition of prayer — combining deep humility with bold confidence, specific confession with rich adoration, and theological precision with heartfelt devotion.

title: The Stewardship of Time
subtitle: Redeeming the Days
description: The Puritans valued time above gold. Receive their counsel on beginning days intentionally, distinguishing urgent from important, guarding against time-wasters, and living with the end in view.

title: The Attributes of God
subtitle: Stephen Charnock on the Divine Nature
description: Drawing from Charnock's monumental work: God's self-existence, immutability, eternity, omniscience, omnipotence, holiness, and goodness — the perfections that define who God is.

title: Grace Abounding to the Chief of Sinners
subtitle: Bunyan's Spiritual Autobiography
description: Bunyan's raw, honest account of his years-long battle with doubt, despair, and the fear of the unpardonable sin — and the grace that proved sufficient for the chief of sinners.

title: The Discipline of Suffering
subtitle: Finding God in the Furnace
description: Practical counsel from the Puritans on navigating suffering: do not waste it, remember it is temporary, cling to promises, pour out your heart honestly, and keep your eyes on Christ.

title: The Doctrine of Adoption
subtitle: The Privilege of Being God's Children
description: Adoption gives the believer a new name, a new family, a new inheritance, and a new relationship with God. Explore the privilege of crying 'Abba, Father' — not in fear but in childlike confidence.

title: The Mystery of Providence
subtitle: John Flavel on Tracing God's Hand
description: Flavel trains believers to recognize God's hand in daily life: keeping a providence journal, noting divine timing, tracing unexpected means, and trusting the Weaver who sees the full tapestry.

title: The Tongue — Governing the Most Dangerous Member
subtitle: Practical Counsel on Speech
description: James calls the tongue a fire and an unruly evil. The Puritans identify the sins of gossip, flattery, complaining, harsh words, and idle talk — and offer practical counsel for governing speech.

title: The Doctrine of the Church
subtitle: The Nature and Mission of the Body of Christ
description: The Puritan high doctrine of the church: visible and invisible, the three marks of a true church, the purposes of worship, edification, and mission, and the necessity of membership.

title: The Saints' Everlasting Rest
subtitle: Richard Baxter on Heavenly-Mindedness
description: Baxter's magnum opus on heaven — written from the threshold of death. The full enjoyment of God, the discipline of heavenly meditation, and how the vision of rest transforms present living.

title: The Discipline of Self-Examination
subtitle: Testing the Health of the Soul
description: The Puritans practiced regular self-examination as faithfully as a doctor checks vital signs. Six questions to ask: faith, love, obedience, growth, fruit, and idolatry.

title: The Means of Grace
subtitle: The Ordinary Channels of God's Blessing
description: The three primary means of grace — the Word, the sacraments, and prayer — through which God communicates His saving and sanctifying power. Attend them diligently.

title: The Heart of Christ
subtitle: Thomas Goodwin on Christ's Present Affections
description: Close the month with Goodwin's most tender work: Christ's heart toward sinners on earth is warm, compassionate, and overflowing with love. Your weakness draws Him closer, not further away.
